book: SMITH I / OLD EARTH SECURITY — THE EMPTY RESCUE
conclusions: Severe local lower-limb injury is plausible from direct carrier-to-concrete compression without naming a fracture/nerve/vascular diagnosis.
The manuscript does not need to assert systemic crush syndrome for an isolated approximately 34-minute compression with no systemic signs.
Technical rescue stabilization and controlled clearance followed by non-weight-bearing extraction is medically compatible with cautious field management.
Long rehabilitation and expected lasting functional loss can remain story consequence while exact diagnosis and exact mobility outcome stay UNKNOWN.
